chapter: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
title: 'Desafinado' and Stan Getz's son Steve in Denver
summary: Horace admires how Getz floats notes on Desafinado, and they talk about Getz's drummer son Steve working around Denver and Boulder.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Yeah, right. I think that's another Jobim piece.

Yeah, right. And Stan did a terrific thing on that, man, and he played -- look like when he plays, he floats, you know, the notes just lay there. Sounds like they're so easy, but try -- you separate them and try them. You found out. That's it, you know.
So he's a legend, as far as I'm concerned, and he's a nice guy. I haven't seen Stan. You know he's got -- his son that he's got (inaudible)? here in Denver?
Yes, his son, Steve, plays drums --
Plays drums? I've never met him;
I'm looking forward to meeting him
-- and he's been around Denver and Boulder for several years now.
Does he look anything like Stan?
Not too much. He's -- huh -- my impression of him, he's sort of heavy. He's not really heavy, but he's got a fuller face and so on than Stan.
uh-uh. He's not tall, but he just -- he seems stockier and so on than Stan.
I've noticed he's had a group around playing different places in (inaudible). I read that through [Nat Hentall's] Matt Hammond's column.
I -- well, I've met Steve, of course, and -- in some of the festivals where I've been music director, so -- and I've used him now and then or his
He -- maybe we should turn the tape off, but he's sort of inconsistent. This group may be good one week or one month. The next week, you know, somehow it doesn't come off too well.
There are a lot of guys like that. But he comes from good stock.
Oh, you bet. You can't beat that. Same good stock.
